column1: # wire-fixtures.tsv — the RecvLuaMsg codec contract, shared by BOTH languages.
#   LuaRules/Gadgets/tests/guidance_wire_spec.lua   (Lua must DECODE them, and the real
#                                                    gadget must act on the guidance.* ones)
# Neither side can drift without the other's suite going red. That is the whole
# point: game_ai_guidance.lua is the only consumer of this codec, and it has been
# live and unreachable from the client since it landed.
# FORMAT — tab-separated, one fixture per line:
# Parsed with two rules only, so both a 10-line TS reader and a 10-line Lua
#   * a field column splits on its FIRST '=' (values may contain '=', and one
#   * a key ending in '[]' means the value is a comma-joined LIST, which the
#     encoder comma-joins rather than escaping the commas
# Values may contain anything except a tab or a newline. `%`, `&`, `=` and `,`
# are exactly the four characters parley/wire.lua escapes, and the escaping
# Field ORDER in the wire is sorted. Lua's pairs() order is unspecified, so the
# Lua encoder cannot produce a stable string — the Lua side therefore asserts on
# DECODE (order-insensitive) plus a round-trip, while the TS side, which sorts,
# asserts the exact bytes. Both check the same strings.
